parsed.rationale: Although both records are `type-alias-object` kinds with `shared_field_count: 2` and neither is test, codegen, mock, or sample-app code, they carry distinct names (`PauseWXYC` in `Shared/Intents/Sources/Intents/PauseWXYC.swift` vs. `WhatsPlayingOnWXYC` in `WXYC/iOS/Intents.swift`) that strongly suggest they alias different underlying SiriKit/App Intents types representing semantically distinct user actions — pausing playback versus querying what is currently playing. The structural similarity (both are empty-field type aliases) is a consequence of the App Intents framework pattern, not shared domain logic. Collapsing or redirecting one to the other would conflate two intentionally separate intent handlers and break the intent-dispatch contract.
